officials.name: Ken Cornell
officials.bio: Ken Cornell was born and raised in Gainesville, FL, and earned his Master's degree from the University of Florida. A small business owner and Certified Public Accountant, he was first elected to the Alachua County Commission in November 2014 and re-elected in 2018 and 2022. He is actively involved in various community boards and organizations.

officials.name: Charles "Chuck" Chestnut, IV
officials.bio: Charles "Chuck" Chestnut, IV holds a B.S. in Business Administration and an A.S. in Mortuary Science. He is a licensed Funeral Director and Life Insurance Agent. He previously served as a State Representative from 2006-2012 and a Gainesville City Commissioner from 2000-2006.

officials.name: Marihelen Wheeler
officials.bio: Marihelen has been married to Dr. Paul Wheeler for 25 years and is mother to 3 sons, also serving as a mentor and host family to many students. She has been involved with various local arts and environmental groups, including the Alachua County Education Association and Florida Wildlife Care. Her activist work includes 8 years dedicated to water quality and conservation, which led her to run for the Florida House of Representatives in 2012.

officials.name: Mary Alford
officials.bio: Mary Alford was first elected to the Alachua County Commission in 2020, after many years of volunteering in the community. She has served on various boards, including the Alachua County Environmental Protection Advisory Board and several local non-profit organizations. A sixth-generation Floridian, she holds degrees in Environmental Engineering from the University of Florida and is a recognized expert in sustainable design and energy-efficient homes.

officials.name: Anna Prizzia
officials.bio: Anna Prizzia is Commissioner for District 3 in Alachua County. She founded and currently oversees the UF/IFAS Field & Fork Program and works as the campus food systems coordinator for the University of Florida. With two decades of experience in sustainability efforts, she has worked with various non-profits and community organizations, and previously served in the Peace Corps.

officials.name: Clair Pease
officials.bio: Clair Pease represents Bay County Board of County Commissioners, District 5. A self-taught businesswoman, she has lived and worked in the community since 1993 and is currently the CEO of Emerald View Resorts. She is also passionate about protecting children and families, serving as an honorary board member for the Children's Home Society of Florida.

officials.name: Doug Crosby
officials.bio: Doug Crosby represents Bay County Board of County Commissioners, District 3. Elected in November 2024.

officials.name: Douglas Moore
officials.bio: Douglas Moore represents Bay County’s District 4, which encompasses most of unincorporated Bay County. Doug graduated from the University of Georgia in 1990 with a Bachelor’s of Business Administration in Finance, from Campbell University’s Norman Adrian Wiggins School of Law in 2006 with a Juris Doctorate, and from the Graduate School of Banking at Louisiana State University in 2014.

officials.name: Robert Carroll
officials.bio: Robert Carroll represents Bay County Board of County Commissioners, District 2. He and his wife Sharon have been married for over 20 years and are raising two daughters, Mia and Gianna.

officials.name: John C. Herbst
officials.bio: Born in New York City, John C. Herbst is a veteran of the United States Marine Corps and holds a Bachelor's degree in Accountancy and an MBA. His diverse career spans investment banking, public accounting, and the insurance industry, and he previously served as the City Auditor for Fort Lauderdale, where he established the City Auditor's Office in 2006.

officials.name: Pamela Beasley-Pittman
officials.bio: Pam Beasley-Pittman is a tireless advocate of strengthening unity in her community, known for her integrity, diplomacy, honesty, and effective communication. A Fort Lauderdale native, she worked for the Broward County Sheriff's Office for 32 years, starting as a 911 Communications Operator and ending as an Extraditions Specialist.

officials.name: Steven Glassman
officials.bio: Steven Glassman was sworn in as Fort Lauderdale City Commissioner of District 2 on March 20, 2018, re-elected to a second term on November 3, 2020, and in 2024, he began serving his third and final term. Steve was born in New York City in 1953 and grew up on Long Island. After receiving his BA and EdM Degrees from SUNY Buffalo, he settled in Buffalo, New York where he was an educator for eighteen years.

officials.name: Dean J. Trantalis
officials.address:
1 East Broward Blvd
Floor 4
Fort Lauderdale, FL 33311
officials.bio: Dean Trantalis has proudly served as mayor of Fort Lauderdale since March 2018. He welcomes visitors to the city, known for its stunning coastline, rich cultural diversity, and endless opportunities for adventure, and is dedicated to creating a brighter future for all who call it home.

officials.name: Ben Sorensen
officials.bio: Ben Sorensen serves as the City Commissioner for Fort Lauderdale’s District 4. He brings a mix of enthusiasm for public service, faith, and military experience to his role. Ben is a steadfast advocate for ethical and transparent government, and he works diligently to ensure residents’ voices shape city priorities and progress.

officials.address: 501 President Donald J. Trump Avenue, Hialeah, Florida 33010

officials.name: Gelien Perez
officials.address: 501 President Donald J. Trump Avenue, Hialeah, Florida 33010
officials.bio: Councilwoman Gelien Perez is a proud Cuban-American who was raised in the City of Hialeah, where she attended public schools and graduated from Hialeah Senior High School. She holds multiple degrees, including two Bachelor of Arts degrees from St. Thomas University and a Master of Science in Human Resources Management from Florida International University, and has over 11 years of dedicated public service with the City of Hialeah.

officials.name: Luis Gonzalez
officials.address: 501 President Donald J. Trump Avenue, Hialeah, Florida 33010
officials.bio: Born in Santa Fe, Cuba in 1970, Councilman Luis Gonzalez moved to Hialeah in 1981 and has called it home ever since. After pursuing accounting and earning a degree in Management, he worked in sales and launched a printing company before joining the City's Zoning Board in 2005. He served twelve consecutive years on the Hialeah City Council, including as Council President, and was elected President of the Miami-Dade League of Cities in 2012.

officials.bio: Councilwoman Monica Perez was born and raised in our City of Hialeah. She earned a Bachelor’s of Science in Education from Florida International University and has a background in teaching. She was sworn into office as an elected official on November 8th, 2019.

officials.name: William Marrero
officials.address: 501 President Donald J. Trump Avenue, Hialeah, Florida 33010
officials.bio: William Marrero is a proud son of Hialeah, born and raised in the city he now serves as a City Councilman. A graduate of Hialeah Senior High School and a student of Public Administration at Florida International University, he has been involved in civic life from a young age. As a member of the Hialeah City Council, William is focused on delivering results for residents, supporting working families, and investing in safer streets and parks.

officials.name: Carl Zogby
officials.address: 501 President Donald J. Trump Avenue, Hialeah, Florida 33010
officials.bio: Councilman Carl Zogby was born in Union City, New Jersey, on March 9th, 1962. He is the third and youngest child of Cuban parents, who had migrated to the United States in the 1930s. His father was a World War 2 U.S. military veteran and his mother was a school teacher.

officials.name: Melinda De La Vega
officials.address: 501 President Donald J. Trump Avenue, Hialeah, Florida 33010
officials.bio: Councilwoman Melinda de la Vega was born and raised in the City of Hialeah. She earned a Bachelor’s Degree in Healthcare Management and has worked in health insurance for 20 years. Melinda is actively involved in her community and several nonprofit organizations, including the Hialeah Lions Club.

officials.name: Bill Proctor
officials.bio: Commissioner Bill Proctor has served the citizens of District 1 since 1996. He represents the central city and southside areas of Leon County District 1, and his priorities include affordable housing, quality healthcare, education, and economic development. Commissioner Proctor has also served as Chairman of the Board in 2006 and 2015.

officials.name: Brian Welch
officials.bio: Commissioner Brian Welch has served the citizens of District 4 since 2020. He was elected to the Leon County Commission in November of 2020 to represent the residents of Northeast Leon County. Brian’s priorities include protecting the quality of life and property values of neighborhoods, providing adequate recreational and transportation infrastructure, protecting the environment, and keeping communities safe.

officials.name: Carolyn D. Cummings
officials.bio: Commissioner Carolyn D. Cummings has served the citizens of Leon County since 2020. She was elected to the Board of County Commissioners on November 3, 2020, and holds a Juris Doctorate from the University of Florida Law School. A Leon County resident for over thirty years, she has been a practicing attorney in both public and private sectors.

officials.name: Christian Caban
officials.bio: Christian Caban was elected to the Leon County Commission to represent District 2 in 2022 and currently serves as 2025-2026 Chairman. He is most passionate about serving the best interests of District 2 by prioritizing public infrastructure, economic development, community safety, youth services, and environmental issues.

officials.name: David T. O'Keefe
officials.bio: Commissioner David O’Keefe has served the citizens of Leon County since 2022 and currently serves as 2025-2026 Vice Chairman. Elected in 2022, he previously spent fifteen years overseeing finances for public nonprofits and government organizations. A licensed Certified Public Accountant, he holds degrees from Florida State University and Auburn University and volunteers for various community programs.

officials.name: Nick Maddox
officials.bio: Commissioner Nick Maddox has served the citizens of Leon County since 2010. As the CEO of Family Promise of the Big Bend and Chair of the esteemed Leon County Commission, Nick has proven himself as a visionary leader with a heart of gold, determined to bring about real change and uplift those in need.

officials.name: Rick Minor
officials.bio: Commissioner Rick Minor has served the citizens of District 3 since 2018. He was re-elected in 2022 and is focused on growing the economy, reducing crime, protecting the environment, and ensuring high ethical standards in local government. He also works on projects to improve infrastructure and amenities in northwest Leon County.

officials.name: George Wysong
officials.bio: George K. Wysong, III was appointed as the City Attorney for the City of Miami in April 2024. He began his career with the City as an Assistant City Attorney in November 1994, and has dedicated the majority of his professional life to representing Miami in numerous practice areas. During his time with the Office of the City Attorney, Mr. Wysong has gained extensive experience in nearly every facet of municipal law.

officials.name: James Reyes
officials.bio: City Manager James Reyes was sworn in as the new City Manager on January 12th, 2026, nominated by City of Miami Mayor Eileen Higgins. As City Manager, James is the city’s chief administrative officer, overseeing daily operations, more than 5,000 employees, and a $1.8 billion budget. Prior to this role, he served as Chief of Public Safety for Miami-Dade County and held senior leadership positions with the Broward Sheriff’s Office.

officials.name: Christine King
officials.bio: City of Miami District 5 Commissioner Christine King is passionate about serving the public and has been since an early age. She represents Liberty City, Little Haiti, Model City, Overtown, Wynwood/Edgewater, and the Upper East Side. In November 2021, she became the first Guyanese American to be elected in the City of Miami and the first female to be named Chairwoman of the Commission.

officials.name: Damian Pardo
officials.bio: District 2 Commissioner Damian Pardo was elected to represent District 2 in the City of Miami in November 2023. A lifelong resident of District 2, he has been a community activist for over 35 years, advocating for equality, diversity, and inclusion in South Florida.

officials.name: Miguel Angel Gabela
officials.bio: Commissioner Miguel Angel Gabela was elected in November, 2023, to represent District 1, including Flagami, Allapattah, and parts of Little Havana. He immigrated from Cuba at age 6, built a family and business in District 1, and previously served on the City of Miami Zoning Board.

officials.name: Ralph "Rafael" Rosado
officials.bio: Ralph Rosado is a dedicated public servant and proud Miami native, now serving as the City of Miami Commissioner for District 4, which includes the neighborhoods of Flagami, West Flagler, Little Havana, Coral Gate, Shenandoah, Golden Pines, and Silver Bluff. A graduate of Belen Jesuit Preparatory School and Florida International University, he was both educated and shaped by this community. Today, he is raising his three children in the heart of the district he now represents.

officials.name: Rolando Escalona
officials.bio: District 3 Commissioner Rolando Escalona serves as the City of Miami Commissioner for District 3, representing diverse and historic neighborhoods. Elected in December 2025, Commissioner Escalona brings a new generation of leadership focused on accountability, accessibility, and delivering real results for residents. Born in Havana, Cuba, he was raised in Miami, and his story reflects resilience, hard work, and opportunity.

officials.name: Eileen Higgins
officials.bio: Mayor Eileen Higgins is the first woman elected Mayor of the City of Miami. She leads a results-driven administration focused on building a safer, more connected, and more resilient city where working families can thrive. Her priorities include accelerating housing delivery, modernizing infrastructure and mobility, strengthening neighborhood services, supporting small businesses, and reforming City Hall to operate with clear standards, transparency, and measurable results residents can see and feel.

He has served as a Fort Walton Beach City Council member (2011-2014) and as County Commissioner for District 4 since November 2014, also serving as Chairman in 2023 and 2026. Additionally, Commissioner Goodwin is a personal watercraft safety advocate and lives in Fort Walton Beach with his family.

With a distinguished two-decade career in Aerospace and Defense, he holds multiple degrees and certifications. As Commissioner, he is committed to driving economic development, improving infrastructure, maintaining low taxes, and enhancing county services.

officials.bio: Commissioner Carolyn Ketchel represents District Two, including Shalimar, Okaloosa Island, and parts of unincorporated Fort Walton Beach. With over 38 years as an Okaloosa County resident, she brings extensive federal, state, and local experience in social services policy and administration. She was recognized as Florida's Social Worker of the Year in 2015 and received the 2020 Presidential Advocacy Award from the Florida Association of Counties.

He was elected in August 2020 and took office in November 2020 for a four-year term. Outside of his duties, he serves as a Pastor at Central Baptist Church in Crestview and is committed to responsive, ethical government that protects the quality of life.

officials.bio: Commissioner Sherri Cox is a lifelong resident of Northwest Florida, dedicated to defending constitutional rights and economic opportunity while preserving the region's culture and natural beauty. She holds degrees in Music Performance and Chemistry, and has a successful career in business, political, and real estate development consulting. Deeply rooted in public service, she serves on various committees and is committed to enhancing Okaloosa County's quality of life and economic opportunity.

officials.bio: Ann moved to St. Johns County in 2013 and enthusiastically traded Arizona’s deserts for our beautiful beaches. But her conservative roots run as deep as the Grand Canyon. Ann earned a Bachelor of Science Degree in Business at Arizona State University which she attended on an academic scholarship.

officials.name: Christian Whitehurst
officials.address: 500 San Sebastian View, St. Augustine, FL 32084
officials.bio: A life-long Floridian, Christian Whitehurst has been a part of the Northwest St. Johns County community for over twenty years. As a job creator and business owner, he focuses on economic development, infrastructure, and core services, while also supporting youth, veterans, law enforcement, and first responders. He believes communication is key to serving the community at the highest level.

officials.name: Clay Murphy
officials.address: 500 San Sebastian View, St. Augustine, FL 32084
officials.bio: A resident of St. Johns County for over 33 years, Commissioner Murphy is married to Pamela and they have three children and six grandchildren. He served as a Florida State Trooper for 26 years and is now the owner and operator of a local Sonny’s BBQ. He is also active in local charities and has served his church for over 30 years.

officials.name: Krista Joseph
officials.address: 500 San Sebastian View, St. Augustine, FL 32084
officials.bio: Krista Joseph has lived in Florida since 2007, ten of those years in St. Johns County. She previously served on the Citrus County Hospital Board, helping to turn around a failing hospital. A mother of five, including two U.S. Navy SEALs, Krista is an award-winning author and a frequent speaker to local organizations.

officials.name: Sarah Arnold
officials.address: 500 San Sebastian View, St. Augustine, FL 32084
officials.bio: Sarah Arnold was appointed by Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis in 2021 to serve on the BOCC and was later elected in 2022. She is invested in the St. Johns County community, its schools, its development, and its future, and serves on several boards and volunteers with local organizations. A lifelong Floridian, she and her husband raise their four children in District 2.

officials.name: Kenneth T. Welch
officials.bio: Kenneth T. Welch is the Mayor of St. Petersburg. He is a third generation St. Pete resident, father of two daughters, a graduate of THE Lakewood High School, a fan of the SunRunner and a strong believer that if we keep our eye on Inclusive Progress - it will always lead the way. As Mayor, Ken is working to make St. Pete a city for everyone through his guiding Principles of Accountable Government and Pillars for Progress. You'll often hear him say...."We Are St. Pete!"

officials.name: Kali Dambeck
officials.office: Special Assistant – Chief of Staff Doyle Walsh

officials.name: Curtis Richardson
officials.bio: Curtis Richardson, Mayor Pro Tem - Seat 2, was born in Jacksonville and reared in Green Cove Springs, Florida. He graduated with honors in 1974 and obtained a B.S. degree in Psychology from Florida State University, later earning a Masters degree in Counseling Psychology from the University of West Florida and a Master's degree in School Psychology from FSU. His career in public service began with his election to the Leon County School Board in 1990, followed by election to the Florida House of Representatives in 2000.

officials.name: Dianne Williams-Cox
officials.bio: Commissioner Dianne Williams-Cox was born and raised in Quincy, Florida, and graduated with honors from Florida A&M University with a B.S. in Data Processing Technology. She also holds a Master’s in Business Administration from Nova Southeastern University. Her life has been dedicated to community service, voter advocacy, and championing causes for underserved residents in Tallahassee.

officials.name: Jacqueline "Jack" Porter
officials.bio: Jack was born and raised in São Paulo, Brazil and later moved to South Florida, where she lived until moving to Tallahassee to attend Florida State University. As a longtime community builder, Jack has worked tirelessly to advance progress on the issues that matter to our neighborhoods. Most recently, Jack worked at the Florida Department of Environmental Protection as a Florida Gubernatorial Fellow.

officials.name: Jeremy Matlow
officials.bio: Raised on Tallahassee’s south side, Commissioner Jeremy Matlow was elected to City Commissioner in 2018, advocating for citizens and neighborhoods to drive City Hall's priorities. He co-founded Gaines Street Pies and serves on various agencies including the CRA and Capital Regional Transportation Planning Agency.

officials.name: Reese Goad
officials.bio: Reese Goad has worked for the City of Tallahassee for more than 26 years. Prior to being appointed as Tallahassee's City Manager in September 2018, Goad served as the interim City Manager and the Deputy City Manager. Goad has fostered a culture within the organization focused on ethics and delivering high quality, affordable municipal services.

officials.name: John E. Dailey
officials.bio: Mayor Dailey has dedicated his professional life to building strong, vibrant communities. He began his career working for the Florida League of Cities and the National League of Cities. After founding JDA Strategies, he was elected to the Leon County Commission in 2006 and then Mayor of the City of Tallahassee in 2018.

officials.name: Jane Castor
officials.bio: Mayor Jane Castor, the 59th Mayor of the City of Tampa, is a lifelong resident who served as Tampa's first female Chief of Police before being elected mayor in 2019. She was overwhelmingly reelected in 2023 and focuses on improving residents' quality of life through infrastructure, housing, and sustainability initiatives.
